messages:
sophia: Running the periodic RBAC sweep and found an unexpected org-level binding: `group:legacy-oncall@redwood.org` has `roles/cloudkms.admin` on project infra-ops. surprised to see group-level kms admin. did we grandfather this? :confused:

mark: that group was created in 2020. likely an onboarding shortcut. can you paste the exact policy line?

sophia: export shows: `{"bindings":[{"role":"roles/cloudkms.admin","members":["group:legacy-oncall@redwood.org"]}]}` and audit log shows binding created via `SetIamPolicy` by user `ops-lifecycle@redwood.org` on 2021-04-12.

yusuf: if that group contains contractors, this is a problem. first step: snapshot the policy and list group members. commands: `gcloud projects get-iam-policy infra-ops --format=json > /tmp/infra-ops-iam.json` and `gcloud identity groups memberships list --group-email=legacy-oncall@redwood.org --format=json`

sophia: ran the membership list: 12 members including 2 external emails (contractor1@vendor.com, contractor2@vendor.com). tagging compliance.

compliance-bot: group provenance: created via SCIM sync from identity-provider in 2020. Suggested action: require owner attestation before permission changes. Also recommend collecting evidence bundle for audit.

mark: proposed remediation playbook: 1) snapshot IAM + export KMS audit logs, 2) create scoped role `roles/redwood.kms.onsiteAdmin` limited to keyRing `infra-keys` and bind to an allowlist group, 3) migrate workloads to scoped role in canary project, 4) remove legacy group binding, 5) run monthly RBAC sampler and add terraform plan guard.

yusuf: add step 0: identify what is using the KMS admin perms. `gcloud logging read 'resource.type=kms_key AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:legacy-oncall@redwood.org' --limit 100` should show usage, but KMS audit logs use service account callers, so search for calls where protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail equals SA that are members of that group. I'll script membership->sa mapping.

sophia: I've found 3 service accounts that are members via group membership: `ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, `infra-agent@redwood-monitor.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, `backup-sa@redwood-backup.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. decrypts logged in last 90 days for all three.

mark: backup-sa decrypts are only for yearly restores. ci-runner is frequent. we should migrate ci-runner first. create a scoped role with `cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` limited to the specific key names used in CI.

ops-bot: created ticket INC-2026-072. severity: P3. owners: @sophia @mark. link: https://inc.internal/INC-2026-072

compliance-bot: attached artifacts: gs://redwood-audit/incidents/INC-2026-072/iam_snapshot_2650001234.json, gs://redwood-audit/incidents/INC-2026-072/kms_audit_90d.json. request: preserve logs for 6 months for compliance evidence.

yusuf: implementation notes: set up canary in project `infra-canary` and map one CI runner to new role using K8s secret rotation. example command: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding infra-canary --member=serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/redwood.kms.onsiteEncrypter` then update deployment to mount canary creds.

sophia: timeline: start canary in 48h during maintenance window 02:00 UTC. if 5 successful CI runs with no decrypt errors, proceed to bulk migration over next 24h. will post progress.

mark: longer-term: add pre-commit terraform check to fail on any `roles/cloudkms.admin` bindings and an OPA policy denying group-scoped KMS admin assignments. also add a monthly automated attestation email to owners of any high-scope bindings.

sec-oncall: FYI sec-oncall, please monitor for any anomalous KMS operations from the listed SAs during the migration window. I'll add a temporary alert rule.

sophia: starting snapshot uploads now. `gsutil cp /tmp/infra-ops-iam.json gs://redwood-audit/incidents/INC-2026-072/iam_snapshot_2650001234.json` will attach to the ticket.

yusuf: postmortem ask: please capture how the legacy binding was introduced (manual grant vs automation), whether group contained external members, what keys were accessible, and list of mitigations (scoped roles, terraform guardrail, monthly sampler, attestation). compliance needs the bundle for the quarterly review.

mark: thanks team. will document and follow up on automation tasks after migration. :lock:
